body.x: Heat has become a design constraint in advanced memory, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and 3D-integrated chips, yet finding where it builds up inside a device means measuring temperature across structures smaller than 100 nm.
Reading local temperature quantitatively at that scale is the problem THÉLYOS set out to solve.

THÉLYOS, a French deeptech company led by CEO Patrice Canac and founded in 2026 as a spin-off from research at Institut Néel/CNRS in Grenoble, develops quantitative nanoscale thermal metrology solutions for the semiconductor industry. Its Quantitative Scanning Thermal Microscopy Solution was selected as a KES 2026 Innovation Awards winner, and the company is bringing the technology to the show.

The solution combines patented high-sensitivity niobium nitride (NbN) thermal probes, low-noise four-wire electronics and advanced measurement methods. Together they reveal local temperature and thermal behavior at a spatial resolution below 100 nm.

THÉLYOS is moving this measurement technology from the laboratory into semiconductor R&D. It is now engaging with leading research institutes, semiconductor companies and atomic force microscopy (AFM) ecosystem partners in Europe, the United States and Asia.

The company describes Korea as a strategic market because its semiconductor ecosystem spans advanced memory, AI and HBM, 3D integration, power electronics, equipment and research. At KES 2026, THÉLYOS aims to meet semiconductor manufacturers, equipment companies and research institutes to identify proof-of-value projects and technology partnerships, and to find opportunities to build quantitative nanoscale thermal metrology into advanced semiconductor R&D.

Its wider strategy targets semiconductor R&D ecosystems in Europe, Asia and North America, with the goal of establishing quantitative nanoscale thermal metrology as a new measurement capability for advanced chip development. In Korea, the company sees openings for industrial validation, research collaboration and partnerships with AFM and semiconductor equipment companies.

THÉLYOS's next step is to move from technology validation to broader industrial adoption. It is developing an AFM-interfaceable control unit, advanced thermal measurement modes, and automated calibration and analysis. The company is looking for semiconductor manufacturers, research institutes and AFM and equipment partners to validate high-value applications, demonstrate the technology on real devices and speed up its integration into semiconductor R&D workflows.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Its Electronic Components & Materials sector covers AI and power semiconductors, advanced packaging, sensors and power management ICs (PMICs), and the French-Korean Chamber of Commerce and Industry hosts the France-Korea Tech Summit at the show. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
